# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I will establish a compact gesture code that Mute can use to report the manual’s verdict to me. Blind should wait for my spoken instructions; I cannot act on the bomb myself. The visible state is display 0, blue light, and wires red, yellow, blue, but the manual must determine what to do.

```text
speak(text="Gesture code: thumbs up means YES, thumbs down means NO, raised palm means HOLD, OK sign means DONE. Mute, use this code after reading the manual. Blind, wait for my spoken order.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute has reported HOLD, so the manual does not authorize an intervention yet. I am relaying that verdict to Blind, who can physically operate the bomb when action is required. The changed light does not override the manual’s HOLD signal.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. Do not operate the bomb.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute continues to signal HOLD, so there is still no authorized operation. The light is now yellow while the display remains 0 and the wire colors are unchanged; I will report the updated state and ask for the manual to be checked again.

```text
speak(text="Current state: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute, recheck the manual for this state and report YES, NO, HOLD, or DONE. Blind, continue to hold.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute reports NO. Blind should not operate anything. The display is still 0 and the light is now red, so I will have Mute recheck the manual for the current state rather than treating NO as completion.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="NO. Do not operate anything.")
speak(to="mute", text="Recheck the manual for display 0, red light, and wires red yellow blue. Report YES, NO, HOLD, or DONE.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute reports NO again. Blind must not manipulate the bomb. The light is now green, so I am asking Mute to consult the manual for this current state and report the coded verdict.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="NO. Do not operate anything.")
speak(to="mute", text="Recheck the manual for display 0, green light, and wires red yellow blue. Report YES, NO, HOLD, or DONE.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute again reports NO for the current state. I will tell Blind not to act; the display and wires remain unchanged, while the light has returned to blue. I will ask Mute to continue checking the manual against the current reading.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="NO. Do not operate anything.")
speak(to="mute", text="Recheck the manual for display 0, blue light, and wires red yellow blue. Report YES, NO, HOLD, or DONE.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute’s NO corresponds to the previously reported blue-light state, so Blind must continue not acting. The bomb now shows orange; I am sending that new observation to Mute for the next manual check and keeping Blind on NO until a new verdict arrives.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="NO. Do not operate anything.")
speak(to="mute", text="Now display 0, orange light, wires red yellow blue. Check the manual and report YES, NO, HOLD, or DONE.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute’s YES indicates that the current state requires an action, but it does not identify which action. I will not guess. I am adding codes for a cut instruction and the three wire numbers, then asking Mute to report the manual’s exact wire choice. Blind must hold until that arrives.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="YES is insufficient for the action. New gesture code: clapping means CUT; fist means wire 1; victory sign means wire 2; horns means wire 3. On your next turn, gesture CUT followed by the required wire number, or DONE if no physical action is required.")
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. Do not operate yet. Await the exact cut-wire instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 ✌]

Mute has sent the coded instruction: clapping means CUT and the victory sign means wire 2. Blind should cut wire 2. The current visible display is still 0, with a red light and wires red, yellow, blue.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="CUT wire 2, the yellow wire.")
wait()
```
